draft.title: Writing about protest
card: Protest is a framework of ideas. A writer explores why people speak out, resist or refuse, and the forms protest takes.
A protest starts from a cause, such as a wrong, a fear or a belief. A piece can show what pushes a person to act.
Protest can be loud, such as a rally or a chant, or quiet, such as a refusal, a silence or a stitched banner. A piece can explore more than one form.
A piece about protest still needs a clear point of view. It can be a story, a speech, a poem or a persuasive piece, and it can show the cost or the effect of speaking out.
draft.remember: Writing about protest explores why people resist and how they show it, loudly or quietly.

a.q: Which piece of writing is exploring the framework of protest?
opts: A girl refuses to sign a petition she thinks is unfair
A boy wins a trophy at his school sports carnival
A family moves to a new city because of a job
A child invents a game with a cardboard box
a.why: The girl refuses to go along with something she sees as unfair, which is a form of resistance. The other pieces are about sport, moving and play, so they fit other frameworks. A story about sport may involve conflict, but it is not about speaking out or refusing.
a.clue: Look for a character who speaks out, resists or refuses.

b.q: Priya writes a short story set in a factory. The workers say nothing for one whole shift, and the manager cannot work out why. What is she exploring?
opts: A quiet form of protest, shown through silence
A loud form of protest, shown through a rally
A game, shown through the workers' imagination
A personal journey, shown through one worker's growth
b.why: The workers use silence to show that something is wrong, so Priya is exploring a quiet form of protest. It is not loud, as there is no rally or chant. Silence can be a form of protest, so the story is not just about people being shy or tired.
b.clue: Think about what the silence is doing for the workers.

a.best: A girl refuses to sign a petition she thinks is unfair

b.best: A quiet form of protest, shown through silence

a.q: Which piece of writing is exploring the framework of protest?
opts: A nurse writes to the paper about unsafe hospital wards
A boy wins a trophy at his school sports carnival
A family moves to a new city for a parent's job
A child invents a game with a cardboard box
a.why: The nurse speaks out publicly about something she sees as wrong, which is a form of protest. The other pieces are about sport, moving and play, so they fit other frameworks. A sports story may involve rivalry, but winning a trophy is not speaking out against anything.
a.clue: Which character is pushing back against something?

b.q: In Priya's story, factory workers say nothing for a whole shift after a coworker is sacked without warning. What does this show?
opts: Quiet resistance to the sacking of their coworker
Not protest, since protest needs a rally or a chant
Tiredness, since the workers have had a long day
A private game the workers play to pass the time
b.why: The sacking is the cause, and the silence is the workers' quiet way of resisting it. Protest can be quiet as well as loud, so the lack of a rally or chant does not stop it being protest.
b.clue: Think about what came just before the shift.

a.best: A nurse writes to the paper about unsafe hospital wards

b.best: Quiet resistance to the sacking of their coworker
